A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same INTUITOR/RLIF research. Their main text, equations, 16 figures, 10 tables, and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison; the changed pagination does not reflect missing material.

before.justification: v3 reports original model-training experiments, benchmark evaluations, ablations, statistical analyses, and generated-response case studies in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experimental results, including benchmark tables, training curves, reward comparisons, and Appendix C case studies.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same self-certainty reward, group-normalized advantages, clipped GRPO objective, and KL regularization. The online/offline scoring procedures and appendix optimization variants are also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions train on MATH and Codeforces and evaluate GSM8K, MATH500, LiveCodeBench v6, CRUXEval-O, MMLU-Pro, and AlpacaEval 2.0. The sequential-domain and failure scenarios in Appendix B are retained.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain identical comparator membership, including base models, GRPO, and GRPO-PV where originally evaluated. Appendix B retains entropy, random-reward, raw/normalized log-probability, and direct-optimization comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 4 and the appendices retain the same training splits, model configurations, budgets, prompting, greedy decoding, and evaluation metrics. Table 10 settings and the protocols for supplementary experiments are unchanged.

E4.justification: The early-learning, online/offline reward, KL-penalty, rollout-size, alternative-reward, optimization, combined-training, variance, and failure analyses already appear in v3. v5 retains them and the same Appendix C response examples.

E5.justification: Figure 8 retains the same Mann–Whitney U tests, p-values, and effect sizes. Appendix B.9 and Figure 16 retain correctness-variance reporting, with no added or revised run-count, seed, or uncertainty-estimation information.

E6.justification: The benchmark entries, plotted results, and qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains INTUITOR's Qwen2.5-3B scores of 0.792 on GSM8K, 0.612 on MATH500, 0.153 on LCB, and 0.416 on CRUXEval-O.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 removes the inference from KL argument order that self-certainty is mode-seeking while entropy is mode-covering. This withdraws a limited mathematical characterization; the self-certainty definition, optimization equations, and appendix formulas remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims: learning from intrinsic self-certainty without external rewards, comparable mathematical performance, competitive or better transfer, and emergent structured reasoning.

C2.justification: Removing the mode-seeking/mode-covering distinction in Section 3.2 narrows the explanation for why self-certainty differs from entropy. Interpretations of the experiments and limitations concerning prior knowledge, hyperparameter sensitivity, and reward exploitation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Both versions provide the same code-access statement, software references, A100 hardware information, Table 10 hyperparameters, and Appendix C.1 prompts. Existing discrepancies between narrative settings and Table 10 are retained rather than corrected.

R1.justification: The related-work discussions and reference list retain the same works and research positioning. Differences in citation wrapping and URL line breaks do not introduce or remove references.

P1.justification: There are limited wording edits in Sections 3.2 and 5, a shortened Table 1 caption, an updated author email, and paragraph-formatting changes. The section order, appendix organization, and almost all prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Document-wide changes to margins and text-block geometry resize and redistribute displays throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 2 moves alongside Section 5.1, and Table 10 moves before Appendix C. All figures and tables are retained, with unchanged graphical content and table membership.

improvement.justification: v5 modestly improves precision by removing the unsupported categorical mode-seeking/mode-covering explanation in Section 3.2 while preserving the explicit reward definition. The extensive reformatting largely redisplays existing material; empirical support, limitations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
